title: NUMBERVALUE falls back to the host VALUE grammar for letter/digit separators and rounds 15-digit mantissas by reciprocal
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527 (en-ZA), when given a separator outside ".", ",", " ", or U+00A0 on text its own reader refuses, NUMBERVALUE strips group_separator before the first decimal_separator, replaces decimal_separator with the host decimal separator, and parses via the host VALUE grammar (e.g. NUMBERVALUE("%1e3", ".", "e") is 0.13, while NUMBERVALUE("1e-3", "e", ",") is #VALUE!). On 15-digit mantissas such as "600757912143053e-27", Excel divides by 10^27 rather than correctly rounding to binary64, differing by 1 ULP on 48 of 366 fn12 pinned rows. In compatibility-version-1 workbooks, @NUMBERVALUE evaluates to #NAME?.
basis: Measured across jnt_text_formats (rows 40-46), 366 fn12 rows (crates/calc-func/tests/witnesses/NUMBERVALUE.json), and 30 letter/digit-separator controls in dc-iuwct.35; matched across 2,835/2,835 full-bank and 318/366 pinned rows.
